elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained §13: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)... No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement." Ownership stays with Vendor; the redline deliberately targets the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; §13 expressly negates transfer of title to Sparkling.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §13 retained: Garman owns all intellectual property rights in the Work and related materials, logos and names.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Amended §2: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and non-exclusive licence to use, modify and sublicense... (i) the Software... and (ii) the Documentation."

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Amended §2 includes "royalty-free"; the additional-fee sentence for non-Authorized Locations was deleted, so no residual royalty mechanic contradicts it.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The only data sentence added is a limit on Garman's licence ("Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services"). There is no affirmative statement that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in its data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." No broader exploitation right (resale, independent use, "purposes contemplated") is retained; §4(b) conversion work is service delivery.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §13 vests sole ownership in Garman; no joint-ownership language appears in the cited or rendered text, so the element's condition (joint ownership to be deleted) does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Already met and preserved: §13 "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)..."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Amended §2 grants a "perpetual" licence; the term/termination-conditioned character of the old grant is displaced on its face by the express modifier.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Amended §2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and non-exclusive licence".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears in the grant and the site limitation ("at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations") plus the extra-location fee sentence were deleted; the retained opening words "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" identify the licensees rather than restate a place-of-use cap, but sit in tension with "worldwide".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" in the grant; the sentence subjecting other-location use to "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" was removed, so no contrary fee mechanic remains in this clause.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "licence to use, modify and sublicense for Sparkling's business purposes".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Grant includes "sublicense... for Sparkling's business purposes", and the contradicting covenant in §3(c) was conformed by deleting "or grant a sublicence of the Work".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the amended §2 grant carries all four modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) plus use, modify and sublicense for business purposes; §3(c) was conformed so the retained covenant no longer contradicts the sublicence right; Vendor ownership of the Work is preserved; and a data-processing limitation was inserted.

Preferred level is not complete: Vendor still owns the Work with no assignment to Sparkling, and there is no affirmative sentence that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in its data (the inserted sentence only caps Garman's licence). The finding correctly targets fallback.

Minimality defect 1: the redline deleted "non-transferable" from the §2 grant. Transferability is not in the fallback checklist and a non-transferable licence is not inconsistent with an express sublicence right; restore "non-transferable" (e.g. "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use, modify and sublicense...").

Minimality defect 2: deleting "at each AS400" removes a hardware/platform restriction that is not required by any selected element. "Worldwide" only requires removal of the Authorized-Locations place-of-use cap and the additional-fee sentence; retain the AS400 wording (or replace the location words only) unless the drafter can show it is a geographic proxy.

Drafting risk to repair: the licence grant is to "the Software... and the Documentation", while ownership in §13 and the §3(c) covenant use the defined term "Work" (which expressly includes Improvements and Modifications, i.e. the Schedule "D" deliverables we pay for). If "Work" is broader than Software + Documentation, the conformed licence will not reach the Modifications/Improvements. Grant the licence over "the Work" (or expressly "the Software, including Improvements and Modifications, and the Documentation").

Residual internal tension to tidy: the retained opening words "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" can be read as a continuing site limit against "worldwide"; consider "for the use of Sparkling and its affiliated companies" so the geographic scope is unambiguous.

Intent preserved otherwise: the assignment/lease/export covenant, the Schedule "D" conversion mechanics in §4(b) and Vendor's ownership statement all survive without contradiction, and no Customer IP or data is assigned to Vendor. Confirm the Fee Schedule does not still price additional Authorized Locations, or the deleted fee sentence could leave a stranded cross-reference.
